title: Wide Plank vs Narrow Plank Hardwood: Pros, Cons and What Works in Sammamish Homes
meta: Wide plank or narrow plank hardwood for a Sammamish home? Compare stability, cost, looks and matching builder oak, plus Wills Flooring's $3.25 install rate.
keywords: wide plank vs narrow plank hardwood, wide plank hardwood flooring Sammamish, 5 inch vs 7 inch hardwood planks, engineered wide plank flooring, hardwood flooring installation Sammamish WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Wide plank (5 to 8 inches) is the right call for most open-plan Sammamish main floors; narrow strip (2¼ to 3¼ inches) wins when you are matching existing builder oak, working in small rooms, or want the most stable floor for the least material cost.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs both at the same $3.25 per sq ft labor rate. The price difference is all in the material, and wide planks cost more per square foot and waste more in cutting.

blocks.html: Most of the Sammamish houses we walk into were built between 1992 and 2012, and most of them came with 2¼ inch strip oak in the entry and kitchen. Now the owners want to extend hardwood through the whole main floor and the first question is always the same: do we keep the narrow look or go wide? There is no universally right answer, but there is a right answer for your house, and it comes down to room size, what is already down, and how much movement you can tolerate.

blocks.text: Wide plank: pros and cons the brochures skip

a.title: Choose wide when
items: The main floor is open plan with rooms over 15 ft across
You want a modern, low-contrast look with fewer seams
You are replacing the old strip oak rather than adding to it
You are buying engineered, which handles width without cupping

b.title: Choose narrow when
items: You are matching existing 2¼ inch oak in the entry or kitchen
Rooms are small or the hallway is under 4 ft wide
You want solid wood over a crawlspace with no humidity control
Budget matters: strip oak is the lowest material cost per sq ft

blocks.text: What actually works in Sammamish houses

items.title: Klahanie and Trossachs builder oak
items.text: These 1990s homes have solid 2¼ inch red oak strip in the entry and kitchen. If you keep it, new hardwood must match width, species and grade or the seam will be obvious. If you go wide, tear out the old strip so the whole main floor reads as one floor.

items.title: Plateau humidity swings
items.text: Sammamish homes see 30 percent indoor humidity by a January furnace and 60 percent in a wet June with the windows open. A 7 inch solid plank moves about three times more than a 2¼ inch strip across that swing. Engineered wide plank is how you get the look without spring gaps.

items.title: Dogs and kids
items.text: Wide plank shows dents more because there is more uninterrupted surface to catch light. Families in Pine Lake and Beaver Lake with big dogs usually do better with a wire-brushed or matte wide plank, or with strip oak in a satin finish that hides claw marks.

items.title: Open plan main floors
items.text: Sahalee and Trossachs floor plans often run 30 ft from the front door to the back slider. Narrow strip across that distance looks like a gym floor. Wide plank at 6 to 7 inches calms the room and makes the space feel larger, which is why it dominates plateau remodels right now.

blocks.text: Where the real cost difference hides

items.html: Material, not labor. A 1,300 sq ft Sammamish main floor costs 1,300 × $3.25 = $4,225 to install whether you pick 2¼ inch strip or 7 inch plank. The material invoice is where wide plank pulls ahead, often by a wide margin.

Waste factor. Strip floors waste about 5 to 7 percent in cutting. Wide plank in a room with angles, a fireplace hearth and a kitchen island wastes 10 to 12 percent because each cut-off is a bigger piece.
Engineered wear layer. Wide plank almost always means engineered. Look for a 3 mm or thicker wear layer so it can be refinished later, which is what keeps it competitive with solid on resale.
Stairs. Stairs are $125 per stair either way, but wide plank treads need to be milled from matching material and take longer to source. A typical 14-stair Sammamish staircase adds 14 × $125 = $1,750.
Tear-out of the old strip. Nail-down strip oak comes up slowly. If you are going wide and removing the original entry oak, expect that line item on the quote.

blocks.text: Mistakes we get called to fix

blocks.title: The most expensive one:
blocks.text: Wide solid plank installed over a vented crawlspace with no vapor retarder. It looks perfect in October and has gaps you can drop a coin into by February. If you want solid wide plank on the plateau, the crawlspace needs a sealed vapor barrier and the wood needs a full acclimation period first.

items: Mixing 5 inch new plank next to 2¼ inch old strip with a flush transition. The eye reads it as a repair, not a design choice. Use a threshold or commit to one width.
Choosing rustic grade wide plank with heavy knots for a house full of clean-lined Eastside finishes. The floor fights the cabinets.
Running wide plank across a narrow hallway. Three boards across looks like a bowling lane. Strip or 4 inch plank handles hallways better.
Skipping the flatness check. Wide plank telegraphs every hump in a 1990s subfloor; strip bends with it. Ask us to check flatness before you order.

blocks.text: How to decide at the estimate

items.html: Lay full boards in the biggest room. Our mobile showroom brings full-length samples, not chips. A 7 inch plank on the floor of your great room tells you more than any photo.
Look at the old oak with us. If the entry strip is sound, matching it with more 2¼ inch oak and refinishing everything together can be the cleanest, cheapest result.
Ask for the crawlspace moisture reading. We check subfloor moisture on every Sammamish estimate. It decides whether solid wide plank is even on the table.
Get width, species, grade and wear layer in writing. A quote for "engineered oak" can mean 2 mm veneer or 4 mm. That gap is worth thousands over the life of the floor.
Confirm the warranty. Every Wills installation carries a 1-year workmanship warranty, and as a Metropolitan Hardwood distributor we can source matching product years later for repairs.

faq.q: Is wide plank hardwood more expensive to install than narrow plank?
faq.a: Not at Wills Flooring. Installation labor is $3.25 per sq ft for engineered or solid hardwood of any width, with a 500 sq ft minimum. The difference shows up in the material price and in waste, since wide planks cost more per square foot and lose more to cuts.

faq.q: Does wide plank hardwood make a room look bigger or smaller?
faq.a: Bigger, in most open-plan Sammamish homes. Fewer seams means less visual noise, so the eye reads the floor as one calm surface. In a narrow hallway the opposite happens: three boards across the width looks cramped, which is where narrow strip or 4 inch plank works better.

faq.q: Can I mix wide plank with the existing narrow oak in my Sammamish house?
faq.a: You can, but separate them with a threshold or a border at a doorway rather than butting them flush. A flush seam between 2¼ inch strip and 7 inch plank looks like an unfinished repair. Most owners either match the old width or remove the old oak and go wide everywhere.

faq.q: Should wide plank be solid or engineered on the Sammamish plateau?
faq.a: Engineered, for anything over 5 inches. Our indoor humidity swings roughly 30 points between winter heating and wet spring, and a solid wide plank cups and gaps across that range. Engineered with a 3 mm or thicker wear layer gives the same look and can still be refinished.

faq.q: What is the most popular plank width right now?
faq.a: On Sammamish remodels in 2026, 6 to 7 inch engineered white oak is the clear favorite, usually in a matte or wire-brushed natural finish. Strip oak still gets installed, but almost always to match an existing floor rather than as a fresh design choice.

faq.q: How much extra should I order for wide plank?
faq.a: Plan on 10 to 12 percent overage for wide plank in a main floor with a kitchen island, fireplace and angled walls, versus 5 to 7 percent for strip. We calculate the exact amount at the estimate after measuring every room and noting the layout.
